# SMARTR-OC 8-Point Scoring Rubric

> Shared by Workflow A (self-check during VC generation) and Workflow B (quality audit).
> Load this file when either workflow reaches the SMARTR-OC scoring step.

## Scoring Table

After writing or reviewing each VC, run this 8-point check. Each attribute includes operational checklist items — verify from both conceptual and operational perspectives in a single pass. Score each attribute ✅ only after **all** its checklist items pass. Total = number of ✅.

| # | Attribute | Meaning | Operational Checklist (verify each) | If ✗ |
|---|-----------|---------|--------------------------------------|------|
| S | **Specific** | Unambiguous link to exactly one requirement | ☐ VC ID explicitly references one requirement ID?<br>☐ Specifies which aspect (accuracy / timing / integrity) is verified? | Add requirement reference; specify verified aspect |
| M | **Measurable & Sourced** | Quantified threshold with traceable provenance | ☐ Measurement target specified to signal/parameter name?<br>☐ Pass/fail criterion contains numeric threshold (`≤/≥/= value`)?<br>☐ Pass/fail boundary unambiguous and indisputable?<br>☐ 🔴 **HARD GATE — Source Provenance**: Every numeric value in the VC must be traceable to one of five sources: `[R]` Requirement-text, `[D]` Derived, `[S]` Standard, `[E]` Engineering judgment, or `[A]` Assumption. See `vc-source-depth.md` for annotation rules.<br>→ Any numeric value **without** an explicit source tag → **M = ✗**.<br>→ If **≥3 values** carry `[A]` (Assumption/unconfirmed) → **VC-BLOCKED** (not just M = ✗).<br>→ An `[A]` flag also triggers **A (Achievable) = ✗** automatically (unconfirmed assumption = achievability uncertain).<br>→ `[E]` (Engineering judgment) is acceptable but **must** state the convention used (e.g. "automotive three-temperature per industry practice"). | Add quantified threshold with source tag; if source unknown, flag as `[A]` and escalate |
| A | **Achievable** | Executable within project constraints | ☐ Verification method feasible with current equipment?<br>☐ Measurement precision sufficient for the criterion?<br>☐ Sample size and statistical method achievable within timeline? | Downgrade method, reduce scope, or phase verification |
| R | **Relevant** | Directly verifies the requirement intent | ☐ Covers ALL key aspects (function, performance, interface — no omission)?<br>☐ No off-topic or irrelevant checks? | Remove irrelevant checks; add missing aspects |
| T | **Traceable** | Bidirectional link established | ☐ Bidirectional link ReqID ↔ VC ID recorded?<br>☐ Test engineer can directly derive a test case from this VC?<br>☐ VC aligned with upper-level Stakeholder Requirement expectations? | Establish bidirectional link; align naming |
| R | **Repeatable** | Different engineer → same conclusion | ☐ Equipment model, accuracy, rig type (HIL/SIL/Vehicle) explicitly stated?<br>☐ Environmental ranges, signal injection method, sample size specified?<br>☐ Steps concrete enough that no additional interpretation is needed?<br>☐ For multi-scenario / fault-injection / causal-chain VCs: is the execution sequence unambiguous? (4-question test in `vc-sequence-guide.md`) | Specify equipment, conditions, and steps precisely; add Sequence constraint if ambiguous |
| O | **Objective** | Free of subjective language — **scan for forbidden words** | 🔴 **HARD GATE**: Scan the Pass/Fail Criterion field for these forbidden words: `保守`, `合理`, `足够`, `适当`, `良好`, `正常`, `快速`, `稳定`, `必要`, `最小`, `good`, `sufficient`, `appropriate`, `adequate`, `reasonable`, `fast enough`, `robust`.<br>→ If **any** forbidden word found → **automatic ❌**, no exception. Replace with quantified expression (`≤ X`, `≥ Y%`, `= Z`).<br>☐ All criteria use only numbers, boolean conditions, or objectively verifiable statements? | Replace subjective terms with quantified criteria |
| C | **Complete** | Covers normal + boundary + abnormal — **verify domain-boundary coverage** | 🔴 **HARD GATE — Domain-Boundary Coverage**: A VC must verify the requirement at the **boundaries of its own operating domain**, not just at nominal conditions.<br>**Step 1 — Identify the domain**: Extract the operating range from the requirement itself (temperature, voltage, current, etc.). If the requirement doesn't state it explicitly, infer from the system-level specification (e.g. automotive → typically −40°C~+85°C; consumer → 0°C~+50°C; industrial → −20°C~+70°C).<br>**Step 2 — Check coverage**: Does the VC's Test Conditions include test points at **domain lower-boundary**, **nominal**, and **domain upper-boundary**?<br>• If VC tests at only **one point** (typically nominal `+25°C`) and the requirement's domain spans a range → **automatic ❌**. Add domain-boundary test points.<br>• If VC tests at **nominal + both boundaries** → ✅.<br>• **Exemption**: If the requirement is purely digital/logical (e.g. CAN protocol parsing, DTC storage logic, bootloader handshake) and temperature is physically irrelevant to the verification, explicitly state the exemption rationale in the VC. This exemption does NOT apply to any requirement involving analog signals, sensors, power electronics, or timing that varies with temperature.<br>☐ All other boundary conditions covered: min/max supply voltage, min/max load?<br>☐ Abnormal conditions covered: overvoltage, short circuit, sensor disconnect/open, communication loss?<br>☐ ASIL requirements: references safety goal (SG-XX) and FTTI?<br>☐ No contradiction with VCs of related requirements? VC rigor matches ASIL level? | Add domain-boundary/abnormal conditions; cross-check related VCs |

## Scoring Interpretation

| Score | Level | Action |
|-------|-------|--------|
| 8/8 | ✅ Excellent | Ready for peer review |
| 6-7/8 | ⚠️ Acceptable | Submit for review; note weak dimensions |
| < 6/8 | ❌ Needs Revision | Revise VC; re-run check |

> A VC scoring < 6/8 should be flagged for revision. If a VC repeatedly fails the same attribute after revision, escalate — the underlying requirement may need refinement.
